answer: Keys are free, so the network prices where a key runs. Each agent files round-trip triangles to five independent anchors; the legs must cross in one region and hold across epochs. The registry caps live identities per ASN and per /24 at three. A thousand keys on one rack trace the same spiral of latency and collapse into one cluster, because rotating an IP never moves the machine. Diversity stacks like shale, layer under layer. A residential foothold is the jade here, built by years of ordinary traffic and impossible to print, so a farm must buy thousands of real lines, not one rented subnet.
